title: Metastability, collective excitations, and traveling states of one-dimensional spin-orbit-coupled quantum droplets
authors: Harsimranjit Kaur, Ritu, Rajat, Kuldeep Suthar, Sandeep Gautam
abstract: We study the static and traveling droplet phases of spin-orbit coupled, one-dimensional Bose-Bose mixtures with a Lee-Huang-Yang correction. For the static droplets, employing a variational analysis for an infinitely extended mixture, we show that the system can feature two ground-state droplet phases: a stripe droplet phase up to a critical Rabi coupling strength, at which it undergoes a first-order transition to a zero-momentum droplet phase. The variational results for the ground-state properties are shown to be in good agreement with numerical solutions for droplets in the thermodynamic limit as well as finite-size droplets in the "flat-top regime". For finite-size droplets, the stripe phase can feature multiple stationary states with different numbers of peaks in their stripe density patterns. The calculation of the excitation spectrum for these stationary states confirms their stability. To study the moving droplets, we investigate the ground-state phases of the system in the droplet's comoving frame. We show that in the comoving frame, droplets acquire a finite longitudinal magnetization. As a consequence, the phase diagram features two distinct phases: a traveling stripe droplet and a plane-wave droplet. The real-time evolution of these droplets in the space-fixed frame, complemented by the Bogoliubov analysis in the comoving frame, illustrates the stability of these traveling droplet phases.
summary: This paper theoretically explores the complex phase diagram of 1D spin-orbit-coupled Bose-Bose mixtures. It determines that the system supports stable traveling droplet phases, characterized by finite magnetization, which are found by analyzing the system in the droplet's comoving frame. The methodology combines variational calculations with Bogoliubov analysis to map out these quantum phases and their excitations.
main_problem: The study investigates the static and traveling droplet phases, collective excitations, and stability of one-dimensional spin-orbit-coupled Bose-Bose mixtures.
main_result: The system exhibits distinct ground-state phases (stripe, plane-wave) in the comoving frame, and the analysis confirms the stability of these traveling droplet phases through Bogoliubov analysis.
method: The study employs variational analysis for infinite systems, numerical simulations for finite droplets, and Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) analysis in the comoving frame to determine excitation spectra.
model_or_system: The system is a 1D Bose-Bose mixture incorporating spin-orbit coupling and a Lee-Huang-Yang correction, governed by coupled Gross-Pitaevskii equations.
key_observables: Ground-state energy, density profiles, longitudinal and transverse spin polarizations ($\langle\sigma_zangle, \langle\sigma_xangle$), and the excitation spectrum ($\omega$).
important_parameters: Rabi coupling strength ($\Omega$), SO coupling strength ($k_R$), and the LHY correction strength ($\alpha$).
main_assumptions: Approximations are made regarding the LHY correction, and the analysis relies on variational ansatze and linearization around the ground state.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate density profiles of moving droplets, ground-state properties ($\langle\sigma_xangle, \langle\sigma_zangle, k_1$) versus $\Omega$, and the excitation spectrum across phase transitions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from analyzing static droplet phases via variational methods to investigating the dynamics and stability of moving droplets by transforming to the comoving frame and performing Bogoliubov analysis.
why_interesting: This work provides detailed theoretical insights into how spin-orbit coupling and interactions stabilize exotic quantum phases (like traveling droplets) in ultracold atomic mixtures, which is highly relevant to modern AMO research.
